Abdi
AB-dye
proper noun
Hebrew Abdi (H5660), my servant — from ebed (H5650), a servant, a bondman, one who serves; the word in Behold my servant, whom I uphold (Isa 42:1).

Biblical Definition

Abdi is a Levitical name of the house of Merari. The first is an ancestor of Ethan the singer, who stood on the left hand in the service of song that David set over the house of the LORD: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch (1Ch 6:44). The second is the father of Kish, one of the Levites who arose when Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the LORD and set about cleansing it — a roll-call of the men who did the unglamorous work of carrying out the filthiness from the holy place (2Ch 29:12). The third is one of the sons of Elam who had taken strange wives and put them away at Ezra's reformation (Ezr 10:26). The name means simply my servant. In Scripture that is not a small thing to be called. It is the title God gives Moses, David, Isaiah, Israel, and supremely the Messiah in Isaiah's Servant Songs; and it is the name the Lord Jesus took when He made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant (Php 2:7).

Origin & Era

A Levitical name of the house of Merari: an ancestor of Ethan the singer, the father of Kish under Hezekiah, and a son of Elam in Ezra's day.

expand to see more

ABDI, Hebrew Abdi, my servant; from ebed, a servant.

1. A Levite of the sons of Merari, ancestor of Ethan the singer.

2. Father of Kish, one of the Levites who cleansed the house of the LORD under Hezekiah.

3. One of the sons of Elam who had taken a strange wife in the days of Ezra.

The word ebed is the title given to Moses, David and the Messiah.

Key Scripture

1Ch 6:44 — "And their brethren the sons of Merari stood on the left hand: Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch,"

2Ch 29:12 — "Then the Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites: and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehalelel: and of the Gershonites; Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah:"

Ezr 10:26 — "And of the sons of Elam; Mattaniah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, and Abdi, and Jeremoth, and Eliah."

Isa 42:1 — "Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles."

Modern Corruption

Servanthood is treated as beneath the dignity of a free man; Scripture makes it the highest title God confers and the form Christ Himself took.

expand to see more

The modern ear hears servant as a diminishment and bondservant as an outrage, and a Christianity that speaks of belonging to a Master is heard as an assault on autonomy. Scripture's valuation is the reverse. Moses my servant is dead (Jos 1:2) is spoken as an honour; David my servant is the LORD's standing designation for the king; and the highest of all the Servant Songs opens Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth (Isa 42:1). The word is not a demotion. It is what it looks like to belong to God.

The apostles chose the title for themselves without embarrassment: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle (Rom 1:1), using the word for a bondslave. And they had a reason. The alternative to being Christ's servant is not freedom but another master — his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness (Rom 6:16). The principle to recover is that every man serves something, that the only liberty available is the liberty of the right Master, and that a Levite named my servant was carrying a better title than most kings.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Abdi (H5660), from ebed (H5650), a servant, a bondman.

expand to see more

Hebrew ebed (H5650) — a servant, a bondman; the title of Moses, David, Israel and the Messiah.

Hebrew Abdi (H5660) — a Levite of Merari; 1 Chronicles 6:44, 2 Chronicles 29:12, Ezra 10:26.

Hebrew abad (H5647) — to work, to serve, to worship; service and worship are one verb.

Hebrew Merari (H4847) — the Levitical house that bore the boards and sockets of the tabernacle.

Greek doulos (G1401) — a bondservant; took upon him the form of a servant (Php 2:7).

Usage

"“Ethan the son of Kishi, the son of Abdi, the son of Malluch”."

"“Of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi” — at Hezekiah's cleansing."

"“Behold my servant, whom I uphold” (Isa 42:1)."
